# M0 · Querying: progressive hints

<!-- GENERATED by tools/build.py from content/*.yaml. Edit the YAML, not this file. -->
Open one level at a time. **Hint 1** gives the conceptual direction, **Hint 2** the SQL technique, **Hint 3** the query structure, and the final level is in [`solutions/`](../solutions/).

## M0-E01 · Titles and authors

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

SELECT names the columns you want, and FROM names the table.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

Separate several columns with commas. Column and table names go in double quotes.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`SELECT "title", "author" FROM ...;`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M0.md#m0-e01).

## M0-E02 · Peek with LIMIT

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

You want to cap the number of rows, not filter them.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

`LIMIT n` goes at the end of the query.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`SELECT "title" FROM "longlist" LIMIT ...;`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M0.md#m0-e02).

## M0-E03 · The 2023 longlist

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

Keep only the rows where a condition is true.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

`WHERE "year" = ...`. A number needs no quotes.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`SELECT "title", "author" FROM "longlist" WHERE "year" = 2023;`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M0.md#m0-e03).

## M0-E04 · Everything that isn't hardcover

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

The format column holds the strings 'hardcover' and 'paperback'.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

`!=` and `<>` both mean "not equal". `NOT` negates a whole condition.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`... WHERE "format" != 'hardcover';` or `... WHERE NOT "format" = 'hardcover';`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M0.md#m0-e04).

## M0-E05 · Recent paperbacks with AND, OR and parentheses

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

Two conditions must hold. One of them is itself an "either/or".

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

Without parentheses, AND binds tighter than OR, so group the OR.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`WHERE ("year" = 2022 OR "year" = 2023) AND "format" != 'hardcover'`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M0.md#m0-e05).

## M0-E06 · Books without a translator

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

A missing value is NULL.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

`= NULL` never matches. SQL has its own operator for NULL.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`... WHERE "translator" IS NULL;`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M0.md#m0-e06).

## M0-E07 · "love" anywhere in the title

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

An exact `=` won't work. You need a pattern.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

`%` stands for any run of characters (including none).

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`... WHERE "title" LIKE '%love%';`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M0.md#m0-e07).

## M0-E08 · Titles that start with the word "The"

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

Which other English words start with the letters T-H-E?

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

Make the pattern require a space after "The".

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`... WHERE "title" LIKE 'The %';`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M0.md#m0-e08).

## M0-E09 · Was it Pyre or Pire?

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

You don't know exactly one character.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

`_` matches exactly one character, while `%` matches any number.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`... WHERE "title" LIKE 'P_re';`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M0.md#m0-e09).

## M0-E10 · Books from 2019 to 2022

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

A range has a lower and an upper bound.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

Use `>=` together with `<=`, or the shorter `BETWEEN … AND …`.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`... WHERE "year" BETWEEN 2019 AND 2022;`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M0.md#m0-e10).

## M0-E11 · Highly rated and widely rated

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

Two numeric conditions must both hold.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

`>` combined with AND.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`... WHERE "rating" > 4.0 AND "votes" > 10000;`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M0.md#m0-e11).

## M0-E12 · Short reads

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

Compare the `pages` column with a number.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

`<` means strictly less than.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`... WHERE "pages" < 300;`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M0.md#m0-e12).

## M0-E13 · The top 10, ties broken by votes

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

ORDER BY sorts ascending by default, and you want the biggest first.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

Add a second sort key after a comma. It only matters when the first key ties.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`ORDER BY "rating" DESC, "votes" DESC LIMIT 10`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M0.md#m0-e13).

## M0-E14 · Reverse alphabetical order

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

ORDER BY works on text too.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

The default for text is A→Z.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`ORDER BY "title" DESC`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M0.md#m0-e14).

## M0-E15 · A presentable average

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

An aggregate function turns many rows into one value.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

`ROUND(x, 2)` keeps two decimals. `AS` renames the column (the name contains a space, so quote it).

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`SELECT ROUND(AVG("rating"), 2) AS "average rating" FROM ...;`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M0.md#m0-e15).

## M0-E16 · Highest, lowest, total

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

You can put several aggregate functions in one SELECT.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

`MAX`, `MIN`, `SUM`, separated by commas.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`SELECT MAX("rating"), MIN("rating"), SUM("votes") FROM "longlist";`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M0.md#m0-e16).

## M0-E17 · COUNT(*) or COUNT(column)?

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

`COUNT(*)` counts rows. What does `COUNT(column)` count?

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

It skips NULLs.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT("translator") FROM "longlist";`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M0.md#m0-e17).

## M0-E18 · How many different publishers?

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

`COUNT("publisher")` counts a publisher once per book. Is that what you want?

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

DISTINCT removes duplicates before counting.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT "publisher") FROM "longlist";`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M0.md#m0-e18).

## D0-01 · The NULL that never matches

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

What is the result of `NULL = NULL` in SQL? Is it true?

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

Comparisons with NULL produce NULL (unknown), and WHERE keeps only rows where the condition is true.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

Use the operator built for NULL tests.

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M0.md#d0-01).

## D0-02 · AND without parentheses

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

Which operator binds more tightly, AND or OR?

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

The condition is read as `year = 2022 OR (year = 2023 AND format != 'hardcover')`.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

Put parentheses around the OR.

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M0.md#d0-02).

## D0-03 · A column that doesn't exist, but no error

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

Read the identifier letter by letter.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

When a double-quoted name matches no column, SQLite quietly treats it as a string literal.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

Spell the column correctly.

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M0.md#d0-03).

## D0-04 · Counting publishers twice

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

Does Fitzcarraldo Editions appear once or many times in the column?

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

Remove the duplicates before counting.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`COUNT(DISTINCT "publisher")`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M0.md#d0-04).
